title: Microsoft Teams: redesigned meeting controls with pin, unpin and reorder
summary: The briefing accurately distinguishes the roadmap target from Microsoft's later rollout windows. The default, tenant-control limitation, licensing requirement and app-pinning controls are supported, including the warning not to use the documented PowerShell cmdlet.

claims.claim: The notice's meeting-controls Targeted Release window is late July to mid-August 2026.
claims.quote: Targeted Release: We will begin rolling out redesigned meeting controls in late July 2026 (previously early July) and expect to complete by mid-August 2026 (previously late July).

claims.claim: The notice's Worldwide General Availability window is mid-October to late October 2026.
claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-October 2026 (previously late September) and expect to complete by late October 2026 (previously late September).

claims.claim: The notice's GCC and GCC High window is late October to mid-December 2026.
claims.quote: General Availability (GCC, GCC High): We will begin rolling out in late October 2026 (previously late September) and expect to complete by mid-December 2026 (previously late November).

claims.claim: The notice's DoD window is mid-December 2026 to early January 2027.
claims.quote: General Availability (DoD): We will begin rolling out in mid-December 2026 (previously late November) and expect to complete by early January 2027 (previously late December 2026).

claims.claim: The sources describe no new permission or identity mechanism or change to meeting roles and policies.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams redesigned meeting controls tenant disable policy PowerShell pin unpin reorder licensing price meter; read roadmap, MC1317197, adoption page, app setup policies and meeting-policies-overview. No new permission, identity mechanism or meeting-role change found.

claims.claim: The sources describe no autonomous behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams redesigned meeting controls tenant disable policy PowerShell pin unpin reorder licensing price meter; read roadmap, MC1317197 and adoption page. They describe layout, user customization and sharing, not autonomous actions.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls; Open questions

claims.quote: Searched: Teams redesigned meeting controls tenant disable policy PowerShell pin unpin reorder licensing price meter; "Teams" "new meeting controls" "disable". Read meeting-policies-overview, app setup policies, Set-CsTeamsAppSetupPolicy and adoption page; no redesign setting found.

claims.claim: No tenant-wide UI or API switch is documented for the redesigned meeting controls.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams redesigned meeting controls tenant disable policy PowerShell pin unpin reorder licensing price meter; "Teams" "new meeting controls" "disable". Read meeting-policies-overview and adoption page. No switch found; MC1317197 explicitly rules out tenant disabling.

claims.claim: The edit path is Teams admin center > Teams apps > Setup policies > policy > Edit > Pinned apps > Add apps.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and go to Teams apps > Setup policies. Choose the policy you want to edit and then select Edit. Under Pinned apps, select Add apps.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams documents Set-CsTeamsAppSetupPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AppPresetMeetingList <list> for meeting-app pins and their order.
claims.quote: -Identity: Name of app setup policy. -AppPresetMeetingList: This parameter is used to manage the list of preset apps that are available during meetings. It allows admins to control which apps are pinned and set the order in which they appear

claims.claim: Teams Administrator or higher can manage app setup policies.
claims.quote: A Teams Administrator or an admin with a higher role can manage these policies.

claims.where: controls[1].governs and note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: For specific-user policies, pinned meeting extensions are available only in meetings organised by users assigned that policy.
claims.quote: When apps are pinned for specific users, the meeting extension is available only in meetings organized by users assigned the app setup policy.

claims.claim: In those meetings, the pinned extension is also available to other participants.
claims.quote: In those meetings, the meeting extension is also available to other participants.

claims.claim: Microsoft says not to use this cmdlet and requires policy creation and modification in the admin center, except assignment or removal from users.
claims.quote: but do not use this cmdlet. We require that all creation and modification of app setup polices (not including the assignment or removal of policies from users) happens in the Microsoft Teams & Skype for Business Admin Center

claims.claim: Changes can take a few hours to take effect after editing or assigning a policy.
claims.quote: After you edit or assign a policy, it can take a few hours for changes to take effect.
